sentences.text: Dennis Walsh (Mr Walsh) is the person being assessed.
Karen Walsh is the daughter of Dennis Walsh and is present during the assessment.
The purpose of the visit is a six-month review of the care package.
The care assessor, Priya Nair, will be writing notes during the assessment.
The assessor will not share information with the council unless there is a safeguarding concern, and will inform the person first.
Brightpath Home Care currently visits Mr Walsh four times a day.
The four visits occur in the morning, at dinner, at tea, and at bedtime.
Mr Walsh reports that some carers are good, and specifically praises Shelley, the teatime carer, for taking her time.
Mr Walsh cannot button his clothes due to hand difficulties.
Mr Walsh does not go up the stairs and sleeps downstairs.
The bed was brought down in March after a fall.
Mr Walsh uses the frame around the house most of the time, when he remembers.
The carers prepare microwave meals for dinner and tea.
Karen brings a proper dinner round on Sundays.
The carers prompt Mr Walsh's diabetes tablets at morning and night.
Mr Walsh reports that Lee, the morning carer, is always in a rush.
Mr Walsh wants Lee to stop coming to him and wants someone like Shelley to replace him.
Mr Walsh used to go to the bowls club but has not attended since his hip injury.
Mr Walsh states that Lee slapped him across the face with an open hand.
Mr Walsh reports that Lee slapped him twice: once last Thursday and once a few weeks back, both times because he was slow getting off the bed.
Mr Walsh reports that Lee grabbed his left arm to pull him up from the commode, and that this happened most mornings when it was Lee.
Mr Walsh reports that Lee grabbed his arm hard on Saturday, which 'really hurt'.
Karen Walsh discovered bruises on Mr Walsh's left upper arm when she helped him change his top on Sunday.
The bruises were four in a row, like fingermarks, on the inside of the upper arm, and were purple.
Karen took photos of the bruises on her phone on Sunday.
Karen asked her father about the bruises and he initially said he'd knocked it, then told her about Lee the previous night.
Mr Walsh said he did not want a fuss and did not want to lose the carers.
Mr Walsh has not told anyone at Brightpath about the incidents with Lee.
Karen Walsh is responsible for shopping for her father using his card and keeps the receipts.
Mr Walsh receives the higher rate of Attendance Allowance.
